source.title: Model Merging Scaling Laws in Large Language Models
source.authors: Yuan-Yi Wang; Yang-Gan Gu; Yi-Ming Zhang; Qi Zhou; Zhao-Yi Yan; Cong-Kai Xie; Xinyao Wang; Jian-Bo Yuan; Hong-Xia Yang

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and appendices. Figure 11's plotted numerical values are not available in the text extraction.
record.tranche_reason: It reports loss scaling during post-training of expert models, a training-stage extension beyond the pretraining setting in the claim. The main model-merging results concern a different scaling axis and are not tests of the claim.
record.gate_note: The main results fit merging loss against expert count and base-model size; those do not test the stated pretraining laws. Appendix F reports expert-model post-training loss trends against model size and computation. Appendix K reports downstream scores against expert count, not model scale or pretraining loss; those results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. Cited pretraining scaling-law results are not extracted as study results.
record.test_reason: The main topic is a merging law in expert count k, which is not one of the versions. But the study also fits held-out CE of post-trained (single and merged) Qwen2.5 experts as L* + B·N^-β over 0.5B–72B base sizes. That is the claim's power-law form in a fine-tuning regime, so it bears on V5. Appendix F adds qualitative post-training loss trends against size and compute.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors' main conclusion is a floor+tail power law for merged-model CE in base size N and expert count k. It holds in-domain and cross-domain, across merge methods and backbones, and can be predicted from three early k points. Separately, they note qualitatively that post-training expert loss improves with size and compute, in line with Kaplan et al. They state that downstream scores plateau earlier and are not claimed to follow the CE law.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures post-training expert loss and merging behavior rather than reproducing pretraining scaling-law experiments. Its main fitted law uses base-model size and merged-expert count, not pretraining parameters, tokens, and compute.
record.method_sensitivity: For the post-training loss result, no method sensitivity is reported. In the separate merging experiments, fitted behavior varies across domains and merge methods; some fitted tail exponents are near-flat, and TIES at λ=1 shows bounded non-monotonicity at 3B.

fits_no_version.finding: Expected CE of merged models falls as A(N)/(k+b) in the number of merged experts, with R²>0.98. The tail amplitude A(N) is near-flat in N for several domains. Subset variance contracts roughly as 1/k.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Held-out loss of weight-space merges of k fine-tuned experts follows a floor-plus-1/(k+b) law, with most gains by k≈5–6.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean downstream benchmark accuracy generally rises and then saturates as more experts are merged. It is noisier than CE, and the authors do not claim it follows the CE law.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream aggregate accuracy under model merging improves with expert count and then plateaus, without following the quantitative CE law.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: For the relevant Appendix F result, Figure 11's plotted values are unavailable in the supplied text; no numerical post-training scaling fits, exponents, uncertainty estimates, or token-axis results are reported. The study's extensive quantitative results concern merging rather than the pretraining scaling laws in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant results left out. The paper's numerous merging-loss tables and plots were omitted because they measure expert count/base-size merging behavior rather than the claimed pretraining laws.

untested.parts: Other modalities (image/video), repeated-data regimes, and transfer. The token axis of post-training is mentioned in Appendix F but no result is reported for it. No fit is given for single-expert post-training loss against compute.
No pretraining runs; held-out pretraining loss is not measured.
The 72B CE is only forecast (a 6–10% further drop), not checked against a measured large run held out from the fit.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Downstream scores are reported against expert count only. The backbones differ in family, so this is not a controlled scale axis.
No comparison of pretraining-law fitting choices. The only robustness note concerns weighting choices in the merging fit.

missing.what: Per-domain joint fits of merged/post-trained model CE against base size N: floor exponent β, coefficients L*, B, and R² for Average, TA and TIES across nine domains.
missing.locator: Appendix H.1 Tables 3–5; Appendix J.1 Table 12; Fig. 4a

missing.what: Macro in-domain CE at k=9 against base size: 0.739 at 0.5B to 0.430 at 32B (−41.9%). Also the forecast of a further 6–10% drop at 72B.
Mean CE against model size at each fixed k, including k=1 (single experts).

record.verdict_notes: The N-axis power law here is fitted to merged/post-trained models built on pretrained Qwen2.5 bases of different sizes. It is a regime extension (fine-tuning), not a pretraining test. The β values come from joint fits that include the k→∞ floor, so they are partly extrapolated within the k axis. The reader's 'partial' states for F1/F2 are not supported by the text, which gives no values. Gemma-2 2B has a k=1 value (0.492) in Table 15, although the text says results are available only for k≥2.

versions.untested_parts: The measured experts are post-trained models, not held-out pretraining runs; no power-law fits of held-out pretraining loss against parameters, tokens, or compute are reported.
No small-run fits are tested as predictors of much larger pretraining runs.
No fixed-compute pretraining allocation between parameter count and training-token count is evaluated.
No architecture depth or width comparison at fixed parameter count is reported for pretraining loss.

The study reports qualitative post-training expert-model trends with size and computation, but does not establish the same power-law form or report numerical fits. It does not test other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning transfer, or the broader regimes listed in the version.
Downstream metrics are reported against number of merged experts, not against model scale or pretraining loss.
No alternative pretraining-law fits or fitting choices are compared. Discussion of expert capacity and merging-fit parameters is not a test of the stated pretraining-law fit dependence.

relationships.condition: Qwen2.5 base sizes 0.5B–72B with domain experts post-trained on DeepSeek-R1 data. Measure is held-out token CE of merged models (k=1..9), fitted on N, across four merge methods and nine domains.
relationships.reason: Based on the text, not the rows (see missing). The floor L∞(N)=L*+B·N^-β fits per domain with β about 0.33–0.42 and R²≈0.98–0.99 (Tables 3–5, 12). At k=9, CE falls from 0.739 at 0.5B to 0.430 at 32B. F1 and F2 are figure-only and cannot determine the form.
relationships.display_finding: The loss floor fitted an offset power law with exponent approximately 0.33–0.42 and R² approximately 0.98–0.99, while nine-expert cross-entropy decreased from 0.739 at 0.5B to 0.430 at 32B.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
